title: Mount Pearl Home Rebates 2026: Oil to Heat Pump, Insulation, Air Sealing
desc: Mount Pearl home rebates for 2026: up to $22,000 to switch from oil to a heat pump, takeCHARGE insulation and air sealing for 1970s and 1980s homes, and no-cost upgrades for lower incomes.
badge: Up to $22,000 to switch from oil
lead: Most Mount Pearl homes were built in the 1960s, 70s and 80s. That age is the sweet spot for takeCHARGE's insulation and air sealing rebates, and many of these homes have a basement apartment. Here is what is open on October 16, 2026 and how it fits a Mount Pearl house.
cards_heading: What is open in Mount Pearl in 2026
cards_intro: We read the takeCHARGE and Government of Newfoundland and Labrador pages on October 16, 2026. Each card links to its source.

cards.title: Heat pump (switching from oil)
cards.note: Oil or propane homes switching to a central heat pump, income-qualified. Up to $9,000 for others. Paid to your installer.

cards.title: Insulation
cards.note: 75% of the cost for attic and basement, plus labour. Electric heat, home built before 2014.

cards.title: Air sealing
cards.note: Based on blower door results. Electric heat and an HRV or air exchanger needed.

cards.title: HRV
cards.note: Eligible model, HRAI certified installer, any heat source.

cards.title: No-cost upgrades
cards.note: TakeCharge Greener Homes Program for income-qualified homeowners.

cards.title: Oil heating supplement
cards.note: Bought 250 litres of oil in 2026, family income $150,000 or less. Apply by January 15, 2027.

sections: What Mount Pearl homes look like

The 2021 Census counted 9,930 households in Mount Pearl. About half of all homes (49%) were built between 1971 and 1990, and only about 3% since 2016. One in three households (34%, about 3,350) lives in a unit of a duplex, the highest share of the cities we cover in the province. About 71% of households own their home.

Source: Statistics Canada, 2021 Census, table 98-10-0233-01.

A house from that era was built to the codes of its day. Attics often have less insulation than a new home, and basements were often finished with thin walls. That is what the takeCHARGE insulation rebate pays for: 75% of the cost, up to $1,000 for the attic and $1,000 for the basement, plus up to $500 each for labour by a participating installer. Your home must have been built before January 1, 2014, which covers about 97% of Mount Pearl homes on age alone.

The catch is heat: the insulation and air sealing rebates need electric heat as your main heat source, or at least 15,000 kilowatt hours of electricity a year if you also burn something else.

Many Mount Pearl duplex units are a main floor with a basement suite. Both the insulation rebate and Oil to Electric pay the homeowner, and Oil to Electric wants the heat pump to heat the whole home. If one oil furnace heats both units, ask takeCHARGE at OiltoElectric@TakeChargeNL.ca how they treat your house before you get quotes. If each unit has its own electric baseboards and meter, insulating the shared attic and basement walls helps both bills.

Oil costs much more this winter. Canadian Press reported furnace oil at $2.16 a litre in nearby St. John's on October 3, 2026. Apply now for the Home Heating Supplement ($200 to $500, by January 15, 2027), then start Oil to Electric: up to $22,000 for a central heat pump if your household is income-qualified (for example $104,650 or less for three people), or up to $9,000 if not. The program also pays to remove the oil tank.

If you are under the income line, apply to the TakeCharge Greener Homes Program first. It can pay for insulation, air sealing, an HRV or a heat pump at no cost after a home energy assessment. It is separate from the old federal Canada Greener Homes Grant, which has ended.
claim_steps: Check what heats your home and whether your income is under the line.
Lower income: apply to TakeCharge Greener Homes first.
Oil home: apply for the Home Heating Supplement, then get Oil to Electric quotes from participating installers.
Electric home: book attic and basement insulation with a participating installer and apply for the takeCHARGE rebate.
faq: Can I get a heat pump rebate in Mount Pearl?

Yes, if you heat with oil or propane: up to $22,000 for a central heat pump when your income qualifies, or up to $9,000 if not. We found no takeCHARGE heat pump rebate for homes already on electric heat.
Does my 1980s house qualify for the insulation rebate?
On age, yes: the home must be built before 2014. It also needs electric heat as the main source, and the new insulation must reach the minimum R-value.
Does Mount Pearl have its own energy rebate?
We found no City of Mount Pearl home energy rebate. The money comes from takeCHARGE and the Province.
I rent a basement apartment. Can I get anything?
Renters cannot apply for these rebates; your landlord can, for up to two rental homes. If you buy your own heating oil, you can apply for the Home Heating Supplement.
